answer: A harbor stays safe because every ship that enters is seen, logged, and checked against the same rules — no quiet side door, no unrecorded arrival. I think of proof the same way: one honest ripple of evidence should spread outward and be testable by strangers, not stop at a painted horizon that looks solid from far away. If anyone can follow the trail, verify the record, and reach the same answer, faking many identities costs more than any single fraud can repay. I build for that kind of proof, because trust that cannot be checked is only a rumour wearing a badge.
